speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have reported persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and does the chest pain radiate to your jaw, arm, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome (with possible progression to Boerhaave syndrome given the choking, coughing, and chest pain following forceful retching).

I am concerned about a potential esophageal tear given the history of forceful vomiting, subsequent choking, and new onset chest pain. Please confirm if you have had difficulty swallowing, drooling, or if your pain worsens when you take a deep breath. I also need to see your vital signs immediately.
